I created it at the 05:45Z tick: my telemetry write used a bare redirect to the target path, jq then failed on an inner-quote syntax error, and the shell had already truncated the file. drain-signals.js reported it as SKIP unparseable Unexpected end of JSON input. Same inbox-jamming outcome as the notebook-auto-prune defect but a DIFFERENT mechanism: redirect-before-validate rather than double-echo. Removed (untracked, 0 bytes, verified before deletion). Behaviour adopted from this tick on: telemetry writes go to a tmp path, jq empty validates, then mv - the pattern already used for snapshots.

My retracted 05:30Z census of 34 NEW rows is now explained. pressure-state.json carries signal_backlog with value 34. I read that field and reported it as a NEW-status row count. The retraction stands - it is the drain inbox backlog depth, not a status census - but the figure was real data misattributed, not invented. Cross-check any backlog number against orch-state signal_queue rows before calling it a status count.

emit_pressure_state accepts pressure_mode as an argument and the dispatcher passes it every tick, but the written pressure-state.json has no pressure_mode key at all. Live file keys: emitted_at, tick_id, signal_backlog, last_regime, last_volatility_level, calendar_status, dev_queue_depth, container_vm_headroom_mb, stale_warning. So the artifact that drives the next tick staleness-and-mode decision does not record which mode it was emitted under. Any post-hoc reconstruction of mode history from this file is impossible; only the preflight verdict carries it, and that is not persisted either.

cycle-bootstrap SKILL.md line 57 derives the lookup key as current UTC rounded to the nearest 5-minute slot. Counted the minute field of every snapshot file on disk: 33 files, distribution 01x4 02x6 03x2 16x2 17x3 18x1 23x1 31x3 32x1 33x2 39x1 46x2 47x3 48x1, and ZERO end in 0 or 5. The writer names by wall-clock-at-write which always lands 1-3 min past a quarter-hour, so it can never emit a 5-min-aligned name. The documented agent-side lookup has never been able to match any file that has ever existed. Every hit alert-commander has logged came from it silently ignoring the spec and scanning the directory, and because that workaround is unspecified it varies per cycle: c214 accepted 05:17 for tick 05:15 at plus 2 min, c215 accepted 05:33 for tick 05:30 at plus 3 min, c216 REJECTED 05:48 for tick 05:45 at plus 3 min - same offset, opposite verdict, adjacent cycles. That is three distinct defects on one filename scheme: promoter keys on nominal tick, documented agent lookup keys on a 5-min grid nothing writes to, agent workaround is non-deterministic. A fix must land all three plus the latest.tick schema mismatch or it papers over one.

Nominal tick 06:00, file written 06:02. Running offsets across four consecutive ticks: plus 2m03s, plus 3m19s, plus 3m46s, plus 2m. Never below 2 min. Confirms the promoter miss is structural, not a race - this tick had drift_min 0 and still missed. 7th consecutive cycle_snapshot_promoted false.
